summary: Acted on the controller's point instead of holding: I opened the one decision-relevant question that had no receipt — what an operator can actually do in the empty-configuration state — and built a self-contained harness for it. The construction-time run reproduced the state (zero servers, no leader in two seconds, staged commit 6, log last index 7) and then tested both documented entry points: live bootstrap refused with 'bootstrap only works on new clusters' and left the configuration empty, while RecoverCluster on the stopped node succeeded and the fresh NewRaft came up with one server and became leader within three seconds. Both events carry a constant correlation key independent of the measured values, and the two comparisons assert whether each path restores the configuration (live bootstrap predicted and observed not to; RecoverCluster predicted and observed to). This completes the repair picture with a negative and a positive: in-protocol via a later configuration entry from a correct leader, an operator restart without the flag, or RecoverCluster on a stopped node — but not live bootstrap and not an incoming snapshot for a node whose log is already complete. A third child investigation records the question under the same parent cause, and fresh execution is requested.
